tier_reason: HttpArena (independent suite) publishes every entry's code and build: frameworks/zix{,-http2,-http3}/Dockerfile (Zig 0.16.0 --release=fast, -Dcpu=x86_64_v3+aes+pclmul+adx), frameworks/nginx/Dockerfile (--with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG') and the libreactorng, libioma, mongoose, h2o, agensio Dockerfiles, run by scripts/benchmark.sh on the Threadripper PRO 3995WX named in site/data/current.json; every req/s figure in the record matches site/data/results/*.json.

corrections.workload: HttpArena profiles across three zix engines: H/1.1 profiles (baseline, pipelined 16x, limited-conn, json-tls, static-tls, latency-1m) on the zix.Http1 URING dispatch engine (frameworks/zix, zix branch 0.5.x); baseline-h2, static-h2, baseline-h2c and json-h2c on the separate zix.Http2 URING engine (frameworks/zix-http2, zix 0.5.x-rc1); baseline-h3 and static-h3 on the zix.Http3 engine, pure-Zig QUIC on std.crypto (frameworks/zix-http3). Each engine runs per-worker SO_REUSEPORT io_uring loops. Load generator (gcannon/h2load/zrk) pinned to CPUs 32-63,96-127, server on the rest; scripts/benchmark.sh keeps the best of 3 runs of 5 s (RUNS=3, DURATION=5s in scripts/lib/common.sh).
corrections.claimed_speedup: baseline-4096: 4,442,329 req/s vs nginx 3,284,513 (1.35x, derived from page data), h2o 3,641,609 (1.22x), mongoose 3,707,598 (1.20x), agensio (C++) 3,558,559 (1.25x), libioma 4,255,834 (1.04x), libreactorng 4,377,377 (1.01x, within noise), Drogon 2,022,710 (2.20x). pipelined-4096 (reference-only profile): 58,761,616 vs libreactorng 43,424,448 (1.35x), nginx 4,037,345 (14.6x), Drogon 7,801,404 (7.5x). json-tls-4096: 1,845,248 vs agensio 1,716,076 (1.08x), nginx 1,313,755 (1.40x), h2o 1,229,462 (1.50x). json-h2c-4096: 6,746,440 vs agensio 4,108,364 (1.64x), nginx 1,691,740 (4.0x). baseline-h3-64: 9,086,240 vs agensio 8,634,941 (1.05x), nginx 4,849,624 (1.87x). static-h2-256: 1,692,045 vs agensio 1,571,021 (1.08x), nginx 802,090 (2.11x), h2o 363,898. echo-ws-4096: 4,469,914 vs mongoose (C) 4,022,433 (1.11x). latency-1m-1024 (fixed 1M req/s, CPU per request): 377.4 s CPU vs libioma 385.5 s, libreactorng 420.3 s, mongoose 436.7 s, Drogon 641.5 s (all derived from cpu_usec in the results files). Not a clean win: baseline-h2-256 14,076,613 vs h2o 16,106,978 (0.87x) and agensio 14,744,015 (0.95x); baseline-h2-1024 14,090,534 vs h2o 15,633,023 (0.90x); baseline-h2c-256 13,956,726 vs agensio 15,185,367 (0.92x), with agensio also ahead at h2c-1024 and h2c-4096 (by 1-2%); static-h3-64 595,586 vs agensio 745,030 (0.80x); static-tls-1024 339,689 vs nginx 720,869 (0.47x), mongoose 611,058 and agensio 1,191,970 (zix last); limited-conn-4096 2,708,192 vs libioma 2,707,029 (equal).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: zix: Zig 0.16.0, zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-musl -Dcpu=x86_64_v3+aes+pclmul+adx --release=fast (frameworks/zix, zix-http2 and zix-http3 Dockerfiles; zix fetched from codeberg by branch 0.5.x or 0.5.x-rc1, not a pinned commit). nginx 1.31.4: custom C module, ./configure --with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG', quictls for TLS/QUIC, brotli built -Ofast -march=native -flto. libreactorng (pinned commit 7a65f8b, patched for Connection: close): gcc -O3 -march=native. libioma (pinned b027f05): gcc-14 -O3 -march=native -flto. mongoose 7.23: gcc-14 -O3 -march=native -flto, OpenSSL TLS, epoll. h2o (pinned ccea64b): clang, CMake Release -march=native -mtune=native, no LTO. agensio v0.1.0-alpha.23: CMake Release, Ninja, -DAGENSIO_NATIVE=ON (Debian trixie toolchain). Drogon: handler built with CMake Release against the prebuilt drogonframework/drogon:latest image, jemalloc preloaded.
corrections.caveats: The margin over the fastest C entries at baseline-4096 and limited-conn-4096 is 0-4% (libreactorng, libioma), within run-to-run noise; the clear wins are over nginx, h2o, mongoose, agensio and Drogon, which use epoll or Asio rather than io_uring, and on the pipelined, json-tls, h2c-json, h3 and static-h2 profiles. scripts/benchmark.sh keeps the best of 3 runs of 5 s per profile, but the results files record only the winning run, and each entry's file is saved at a different time (zix.json and nginx.json last changed 2026-08-30, libreactorng.json 2026-09-07 after a Connection: close fix), so rows are cross-run comparisons on the same machine; current.json (the CPU and kernel record) is undated. zix itself is fetched by branch name (0.5.x, 0.5.x-rc1), so the exact commit behind the numbers is not recorded. The H/2 and H/3 rows come from separate zix engines (zix.Http2, zix.Http3 with pure-Zig QUIC on std.crypto), not the Http1 engine. The C competitor entries (nginx with a custom C handler module, libreactorng, libioma, h2o, mongoose) are minimal handlers built by the suite maintainers or contributors; nginx is reasonably tuned (access_log off, reuseport, worker_processes auto). The Drogon entry compiles only its handler against the prebuilt drogon:latest image, so its 2x to 8x ratios are weaker evidence. Response sizes differ (bytes per response derived from bandwidth / req/s: baseline-4096 nginx 135.4, Drogon 134.4, libreactorng 108.7, libioma 85.8, mongoose 72.5, zix 62.9; baseline-h3 zix about 7.6, agensio about 17.4, nginx about 76), so zix writes the fewest bytes per request. In static-tls zix sends about 11.9 KB per response against about 3.1 KB for nginx and agensio (derived), consistent with nginx (gzip_static, brotli_static) and agensio serving precompressed variants that zix does not, so that profile is not like-for-like either way. The pipelined profile is reference-only in HttpArena's composite score. The zix README only links to HttpArena badges and gives no numbers.
corrections.why_faster: Architecture, not the language: per-worker SO_REUSEPORT io_uring loops with a comptime router and a staged send sink (HttpArena meta.json), minimal response headers, and for TLS/QUIC a Zig std.crypto stack built with AES-NI/PCLMUL enabled. The C entries with the same thread-per-core io_uring design (libreactorng, libioma) are within 1-4% on baseline and limited-conn; the large gaps are against epoll-based nginx, h2o, mongoose and Drogon.

notes: Numbers verified against the HttpArena results JSON files for zix, nginx, libreactorng, libioma, h2o, mongoose, agensio, Drogon and userver; tier A holds since every Dockerfile, flag and the CPU are public. Corrections: H/2 and H/3 rows come from separate zix engines; runs are best-of-3 x 5 s, not a single run; more loss rows added (h2o at h2-1024, agensio on all baseline-h2c rows and static-h3, zix last in static-tls, which also serves uncompressed bytes); same_algorithm set false because the large wins are io_uring vs epoll. Shortcomings to record: win over same-design C engines within noise, cross-run result files, unpinned zix version, fewer response bytes than most C entries.

tier_reason: First-party README charts (four PNGs, no tabulated numbers) against nginx 1.24.0 on a stated CPU (AMD EPYC 7R13, c6a.8xlarge), but the scripts behind these charts are not in the repository at HEAD and no compiler flags or nginx configuration are given; an older benchmark/ directory with wrk2 scripts (commit d02397f, removed before archival) lacked flags and a CPU model too.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No numbers in the text; four chart images only. Approximate values read from the charts (not stated by the project). HTTPS vs worker threads: 16 threads about 526k req/s vs nginx about 450k (about 1.17x), 12 threads about 436k vs about 370k (about 1.18x), 8 threads about 359k vs about 334k (about 1.07x), 4 threads about 148k vs about 126k. HTTPS vs body size: 512 B about 152k vs about 128k (about 1.19x), 4096 B about 124k vs about 108k (about 1.15x), roughly equal at 8192 B, then nginx ahead at 16384 B (about 55k vs about 59k), 32768 B (about 34k vs about 41k) and 65536 B (about 20k vs about 23k). Plain HTTP: nginx ahead or equal everywhere, 16 threads about 707k vs about 688k (monolake about 0.97x), 4 threads about 194k vs about 168k (about 0.87x), 512 B about 186k vs about 168k (monolake about 0.91x), equal at 32768 and 65536 B. Older tabulated first-party proxy run (benchmark/README.md at commit d02397f, Nov 2024, wrk2, 4-core proxy, nginx backend): HTTPS tiny 141,883.70 req/s vs nginx as proxy 127,167.08 (1.12x, derived from page data), small 116,831.85 vs 114,350.27 (1.02x), medium 63,390.91 vs 62,450.58 (1.02x); HTTP tiny 161,101.29 vs 187,973.44 (0.86x); against Envoy 1.31.0 (C++): HTTP tiny 4.36x, HTTPS tiny 4.15x (derived from page data, Envoy configuration not tuned or stated).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the README charts. Repository pins Rust nightly (rust-toolchain.toml); the older benchmark/README.md built Monolake with cargo build --release (a release-lto profile exists in Cargo.toml, use not stated) and installed nginx from the Amazon Linux package (yum), so nginx build flags are the distro's and unstated.
corrections.caveats: First-party charts with no tabulated numbers, so values here are eyeballed from PNGs. The win is confined to HTTPS with small bodies (and more worker threads); plain HTTP and large HTTPS bodies favour nginx or tie. The nginx build and configuration (workers, logging, TLS library), whether the charts measure proxying or direct serving, the body size used in the thread charts and the load generator are not stated for the current charts. Monolake's default tls feature uses monoio-native-tls (OpenSSL on Linux), with rustls also available; which stack the charts used is not stated. An older benchmark/ directory (present at commit d02397f, Nov 2024; gone from HEAD) had wrk2 scripts, a three-machine proxy topology with an nginx backend, and a tabulated 4-core run showing only a 1.02-1.12x HTTPS edge and nginx 14% ahead on HTTP tiny; its Envoy and Traefik rows ran stock configurations, so the 4x lead over Envoy is weak evidence. Repository archived on 2025-08-29 with a notice that the project is no longer recommended. Tier C: first-party, partial methodology.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 66 stars, 12 forks; README says it was deployed in production at ByteDance

notes: Chart values in the record check out against the four README PNGs (minor additions: 12-thread HTTPS point, HTTP ties at 32-64 KiB). Found an older tabulated first-party run in the removed benchmark/ directory (commit d02397f) with a smaller HTTPS edge (1.02-1.12x) and an Envoy (C++) comparison; still tier C. Shortcomings to record: eyeballed charts only, win limited to small-body HTTPS, no plain-HTTP win, no flags or nginx config, repository archived.
